findings.description: Long-lived AWS access key ID and secret access key are hardcoded as Lambda environment variables in the Terraform source. These credentials are stored in plaintext in version control and in the Lambda configuration, where anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration can read them.

No kms_key_arn is configured, so the Lambda environment variables (which contain secrets here) are encrypted only with the default AWS-managed key and are shown in plaintext in the console/API to any principal with read access to the function configuration.
No tracing_config block is defined, so no active tracing is enabled, reducing the ability to detect and investigate abusive or anomalous invocations of the function.

The function has no vpc_config, so it runs outside any customer VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security-group egress controls — an attacker who achieves code execution in the function can exfiltrate data freely.
The function uses the nodejs12.x runtime, which is deprecated and no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving known vulnerabilities in the execution environment unpatched.

The assume role policy allows lambda.amazonaws.com to assume the role with no aws:SourceAccount or aws:SourceArn condition, so the trust is broader than necessary and offers no scoping to the intended function or account.
